chunks.text: 56-year-old male, Associate Professional or Technician, resident of Ang Mo Kio, Singapore.
General Anesthesia with Single-shot Dose of Cefazolin for Prophylaxis

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good morning, Mr./Ms./Mrs. [Patient's Name]. I'm [Provider's Name], the anesthesiologist who will be taking care of you during your surgery. I'd like to go over a few things with you before your laparoscopic cholecystectomy. Can you please start by telling me a bit about your medical history and why you're having this surgery?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Morning, Doctor. I've been having a lot of tummy pain on the right side, especially after eating. The doctor said I have gallstones and the best way is to remove the gallbladder laparoscopically.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you for sharing that. Now, let's go over your medications. I see here you're on Losartan, Metformin, Atorvastatin, and Ranitidine. Can you confirm if you're still taking all these medications as listed, and are there any changes?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes, I'm still on Losartan for my blood pressure, Metformin for my diabetes, and Atorvastatin for cholesterol. But for the Ranitidine, ah, I've stopped that one. My doctor switched me to Omeprazole 20 mg daily for my acid reflux because Ranitidine was discontinued.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you for clarifying that. It's important we have the most up-to-date medication list. Regarding your acid reflux, has the Omeprazole been working well for you without any issues?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes, it's been fine. No heartburn or anything like before.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Excellent. Now, about your allergies, we have you down as allergic to Penicillin. Can you please describe the reaction you had to Penicillin?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes, I had a bad rash all over my body the last time I took it. So, I've avoided it ever since.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you for that information. It's crucial for us to know. Have you had any previous surgeries or anesthesia? If so, were there any complications?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, this is my first time. I've never been under general anesthesia before.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Alright, so you're NPO after midnight, correct? And you've had no food or drink since then?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes, Doctor. I stopped eating after dinner last night and haven't had anything since, not even water.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Perfect. Lastly, how would you describe your overall physical activity level? Are you able to walk up a flight of stairs without getting overly short of breath?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: I can walk up the stairs, but I do get a bit out of breath, especially if I go too fast. But generally, I'm fairly active.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you for providing all this information, Mr./Ms./Mrs. [Patient's Name]. It's very helpful for us. If you have any questions about the anesthesia or the procedure, now is a good time to ask.

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, I think you've covered everything. I'm ready.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Very well. We'll take good care of you. You'll see me or one of my team members again before you go into the operating room. Have a rest, and we'll see you soon.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [07:30] induction propofol one hundred twenty milligrams

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [07:32] tube in, grade one view

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [07:35] iv access established, two large bore lines

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [07:40] fluid bolus one thousand milliliters normal saline

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:15] notable hypotension, treat with fifty micrograms phenylephrine

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:45] notable tachycardia, treat with ten milligrams IV metoprolol

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Hi there, how are you feeling after the surgery?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: I'm okay, I guess. A bit tired, but not in too much pain.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good to hear. Can you tell me your pain level out of 10?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Maybe a 3 or 4. It's more like discomfort than sharp pain.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Alright, we can manage that with medication. Are you feeling nauseous or have vomited at all?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No nausea, thank goodness. I was worried about that after reading online.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Great. How's your breathing? Any shortness of breath or discomfort in your chest?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Breathing is fine. I feel a bit stuffy from the tube, but it's getting better.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Understood. Do you remember anything from the operating room or waking up?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Not really. I remember going to sleep and then waking up here. No scary moments, though.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good. Since you have diabetes and high blood pressure, we’ll keep a close eye on your vitals and sugar levels.

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Thanks, I appreciate that. I was a bit worried about how my conditions might affect recovery.
